bullets.text: Writing Java logic that decides how much EC2 capacity Amazon Redshift reserves for operations like patching, setting upper and lower bounds that keep availability high without overspending, and backtesting the policies

Cut AI workflow generation time 65% to under 15s by splitting one large Claude skill into smaller sub-skills that call Python tools for search and validation, after CloudWatch and OpenSearch latency logs showed where time went

Because the 270K+ row PostgreSQL workflow table had strict access limits, precomputed popular workflows into a category tree that the Claude skill searches first, with Redis caching full workflows to cut database queries

Rebuilt the legacy tool developers use to create test-data workflows as a React and TypeScript Electron app with a visual React Flow editor and Jest-tested validation, and 90% of 30+ surveyed developers preferred it

Cut end-to-end latency 34% on the pipeline that sends a 6,000+ document scraped research corpus to model inference by replacing scraper-to-S3-to-Lambda staging with Amazon Kinesis streams feeding AWS Lambda

Deployed a space-topic research tool for Amazon Leo's public-policy team and set it up for handoff with AWS CDK infrastructure-as-code and GitHub Actions CI/CD, so Leo engineers new to the project now maintain it on AWS Fargate

Automated retraining for a production Amazon Bedrock classifier that rates research documents by importance: on an EventBridge schedule a larger LLM grades its ratings, and fine-tuning runs only when the grades shift past a threshold
Cut research-environment setup time 30% by pinning dependencies with uv and packaging the environment in Docker so every machine gets an identical setup

Co-founded a 110+ member student product studio that has shipped 5 live products, and personally built Redis caching in front of the Prisma ORM queries for one, Tortuga, a class scheduler with 20,000+ visits in its first 30 days

Built a C++17 order book and matching engine and replayed 50.9M real IEX exchange messages through it without ever resyncing to the exchange's book, matching 99,122 of 99,123 fills and 100% of top-of-book prices

Implemented B+ tree and LSM-tree backends for the engine's event log and benchmarked them on identical 2M-record workloads: the B+ tree gave 12.8x the read throughput and 22x faster range summaries for 27% more disk
Sustained 1.26M events/sec end-to-end over the full replay, keeping each price level's orders in a std::list FIFO inside a std::map and a hash map from order ID to list iterator for O(1) cancels
